6 - [Negative] Verify PRODUK mega-menu categories match the Figma spec exactly
CONFIRMED REAL MISMATCH — Figma's "Menu Dropdown - Atap" frame specifies 5 category links: Dinding, Atap Metal, Rangka Baja Ringan, Interior, Aksesoris. Live renders 6 links with different wording: Atap, Atap Pasiran, Dinding, Baja Ringan, Interior, Aksesoris — "Atap Metal" has been split into two separate live categories ("Atap" + "Atap Pasiran") and "Rangka Baja Ringan" is shortened to "Baja Ringan" live. Flagged for the client to confirm whether this is an intentional catalog restructuring (plausible — real catalogs commonly outgrow an early mockup) or a design-sync gap; not confidently a "bug" either way.

🔍 Root Cause
The Figma "Menu Dropdown - Atap" frame specifies 5 PRODUK categories: Dinding, Atap Metal, Rangka Baja Ringan, Interior, Aksesoris. The live PRODUK mega-menu instead renders 6 categories: Atap, Atap Pasiran, Dinding, Baja Ringan, Interior, Aksesoris. "Atap Metal" appears to have been split into two live categories ("Atap" + "Atap Pasiran"), and "Rangka Baja Ringan" has been shortened to "Baja Ringan". This is a content/catalog-structure drift between the design spec and the live category tree, not a rendering or JS defect — the mega-menu itself opens and links correctly.
❌ Problematic Code
- Live PRODUK mega-menu links (captured via outerHTML):
- <a href="/produk/atap-berwarna.html">Atap</a>
- <a href="/produk/atap-pasiran.html">Atap Pasiran</a>
- <a href="/produk/dinding.html">Dinding</a>
- <a href="/produk/rangka-baja-ringan.html">Baja Ringan</a>
- <a href="/produk/interior.html">Interior</a>
- <a href="/produk/aksesoris.html">Aksesoris</a>
✅ Fixed Code
No code fix applies — this is a content decision, not a bug. Two possible resolutions depending on which source is authoritative:
- If the live 6-category structure is the intended, up-to-date catalog: update the Figma "Menu Dropdown - Atap" frame's text layers to match (split "Atap Metal" into "Atap"/"Atap Pasiran", rename "Rangka Baja Ringan" to "Baja Ringan").
- If the Figma 5-category structure is correct: raise a catalog/CMS ticket to consolidate the live categories back down to 5.
📋 What To Do
Flag this to the client/design team for an explicit decision on which category structure is authoritative, since a real catalog naturally outgrowing an early mockup is plausible but unconfirmed. Once confirmed, update whichever source (Figma spec or live catalog config) is stale.

🖼️ Live Page Screenshot — the actual front-end element click to zoom
🔍 Root Cause
The header search-suggest AJAX endpoint (/search/ajax/suggest/?q=...), wired up via the steelhubSearch({ suggestUrl: '.../search/ajax/suggest/' }) Alpine component, returns garbage/unrelated results instead of real catalog matches. Queried directly outside the UI: q=colorbond (a real, currently-listed brand on this exact page) returns an EMPTY array []; q=atap (the single most core search term for a roofing retailer) returns [{"title":"aaaa","num_results":1}]; q=baja returns [{"title":"bali",...}]. None of these are real catalog matches — the suggest backend is serving stale/seed/test data rather than the live product index for exactly the terms a real shopper would type.
❌ Problematic Code
GET /search/ajax/suggest/?q=atap
Response: [{"title":"aaaa","num_results":1}]

GET /search/ajax/suggest/?q=colorbond
Response: []
✅ Fixed Code
No frontend code fix applies — the frontend correctly calls the suggest endpoint and renders whatever it receives. The fix belongs on the backend/search-index side: the suggest service needs to be reconnected to, or reindexed against, the live Shopify catalog rather than whatever source is currently backing it.
📋 What To Do
Escalate to the backend/DevOps team to inspect the search-suggest service's index. Trigger a full reindex (e.g. bin/Shopify indexer:reindex catalogsearch_fulltext, or the equivalent command for whichever search extension backs this endpoint) and re-verify the endpoint returns real product titles for common terms like "atap", "baja", and "colorbond" before closing this out.

17 - Verify the header remains pinned to the top of the viewport after scrolling
Scrolls to ".benefits-bar", not ".hero" — the hero is the first section on the page, so scrolling "to .hero" from a fresh load never moves scrollY (already in view) and never flips the Alpine "stuck" state that drives the sticky/fixed-header class swap. Confirmed by dumping the header's outerHTML after a .hero scroll_to and seeing the fixed/gradient classes still unapplied. CORRECTED 2026-08-07: the selector used to match on a literal "bg-gradient-to-br" class substring, which the site no longer ships — the gradient is now applied via a Tailwind arbitrary-value class (bg-[linear-gradient(...)]), so the old selector stopped matching anything and this test started failing for a stale-selector reason, not a real regression (confirmed live: the nested header still gets "!fixed" applied on scroll). Switched to a structural selector (header.page-header > header) instead of a specific gradient class name, per the standing lesson to scope by stable structure/attributes rather than bare/arbitrary-value class names.

35 - Verify clicking the 'Trending' Offers filter tab actually filters the product grid
CONFIRMED WORKING (corrected 2026-08-07 — see the "CORRECTIONS" note at the top of this file). This section renders 5 separate x-show-scoped carousels, one per tab; an earlier check queried ".product-card" broadly across the whole section, which silently reads across all 5 hidden+visible carousels at once and made every tab look identical. Playwright's real visibility check (waitFor state: hidden/visible) already respects the x-show-driven display:none on each inactive carousel, so a plain href selector is enough here — no ":visible" pseudo-class needed. Confirmed live: "Colorbond® Span 920" (only in the "Semua" tab's carousel) becomes hidden, and a Trending-exclusive product becomes visible, after clicking "Trending".

59 - [BUG] Verify the footer newsletter form shows a response after submitting a valid email
CONFIRMED REAL DEFECT (2026-08-07 reconciliation pass) — the newsletter form has a real action="/newsletter/subscriber/new/" method="post", but clicking "DAFTAR" with a valid email fires ZERO network requests: no page navigation, no XHR/fetch, confirmed via a full request-listener dump across two submissions (a fresh email, then the same email again to also check for an "already subscribed" message). Nothing is ever submitted — no success message, no already-subscribed message, and the backend is never reached so no subscription is ever recorded either.
Failed ▼
syncing…
# Action Expected / Result Status
#01 Newsletter subscription is completely non-functional — clicking DAFTAR submits nothing and no response message ever appears.
⚠ ErrorNewsletter subscription is completely non-functional — clicking DAFTAR submits nothing and no response message ever appears.
🖼️ Live Page Screenshot — the actual front-end element click to zoom
🔍 Root Cause
The newsletter form has a real action="/newsletter/subscriber/new/" and method="post", guarded by an Alpine @submit handler that only calls $event.preventDefault() when the email FAILS a client-side regex check. For a valid email, confirmed live across two full submissions (a fresh email, then the same email resubmitted) that the handler completes with zero console errors and zero preventDefault() calls — yet the native form submission never actually proceeds: no page navigation, no XHR/fetch of any kind is ever observed. This rules out the two most common causes (client-side validation rejecting the email, and a thrown JS exception aborting the handler) and points to something inside the @submit handler itself silently swallowing the browser's default submit action.
❌ Problematic Code
<form class="footer-newsletter" novalidate x-data="{ email: '', invalid: false }" method="post"
      action="https://nsb-dev.kemanastaging.com/newsletter/subscriber/new/"
      @submit="invalid = false;
               if (!/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/.test(email.trim())) { $event.preventDefault(); invalid = true; return; }
               $refs.nlFk.value = (window.hyva && hyva.getFormKey) ? hyva.getFormKey() : ''">
  <input type="hidden" name="form_key" x-ref="nlFk" value="o0pRtny05vYlALx8">
  <input type="email" name="email" x-model="email" @input="invalid = false" placeholder="Masukan email">
  <button class="primary-button" type="submit">DAFTAR</button>
</form>
✅ Fixed Code
@submit="invalid = false;
         if (!/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/.test(email.trim())) { $event.preventDefault(); invalid = true; return; }
         // Leave the pre-rendered form_key untouched when the Hyva helper
         // isn't present, instead of overwriting it with an empty string:
         if (typeof window.hyva !== 'undefined' && hyva.getFormKey) {
           $refs.nlFk.value = hyva.getFormKey();
         }"
📋 What To Do
This theme is Alpine.js/Tailwind, not Hyva — window.hyva is never defined here, so $refs.nlFk.value is being overwritten with an empty string on every valid submit, wiping out the pre-rendered form_key (CSRF token) the server needs. Guard that assignment so it only runs when hyva genuinely exists (see Fixed Code), and separately have a developer set a breakpoint inside this @submit handler and step through a real valid-email submission to confirm exactly where the native submit gets swallowed, since no JS error or preventDefault() was observed to explain it directly. After the fix, re-verify both that a NEW email shows a success message and that RESUBMITTING the same email shows an "already subscribed" message, and that the email is actually persisted server-side.
